intro: Bristol rewards visitors with a walkable harbourside, lively food markets and easy trips into the countryside. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; the Severn Beach rail line links Temple Meads with Clifton Down and Avonmouth.
Buses cover the city centre and suburbs; contactless tap fares are around £2-3.
Taxis and private hire are common; Uber and Bolt both operate in Bristol.
Driving is slow in the centre; use Park and Ride sites at Portway, Brislington and Long Ashton.
The centre and Harbourside are easy on foot; Temple Meads is about a 15 min walk.
Dott e-scooters and e-bikes cost £0.99 to unlock plus about £0.16 per minute.

clifton-suspension-bridge.name: Clifton Suspension Bridge
clifton-suspension-bridge.hours: Open 24 hours · visitor centre hours vary, check on the day
clifton-suspension-bridge.tip: Walk across for free views over the Avon Gorge, then loop back through Clifton Village.

ss-great-britain.name: SS Great Britain
ss-great-britain.price_text: Around GBP 20 adult · check current prices online
ss-great-britain.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–17:00 · check on the day
ss-great-britain.tip: The dry dock under the glass 'sea' is the highlight; allow two hours.

bristol-museum-art-gallery.name: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery
bristol-museum-art-gallery.hours: Tue–Sun, roughly 10:00–17:00 · closed Monday, check on the day
bristol-museum-art-gallery.tip: Free dinosaurs and art in one building; good rainy-day stop near the university.

st-nicholas-market.name: St Nicholas Market
st-nicholas-market.price_text: Free to browse · food from a few GBP
st-nicholas-market.tip: Go at lunch for street-food stalls; many close by late afternoon.

brandon-hill.name: Brandon Hill and Cabot Tower
brandon-hill.hours: Park open daily · tower hours vary, check on the day
brandon-hill.tip: Climb Cabot Tower for a free city panorama; the stairs are narrow.

harbourside-walk.name: Harbourside and Wapping Wharf walk
harbourside-walk.hours: Always open · venues have their own hours
harbourside-walk.tip: Walk from M Shed to the ss Great Britain, then eat at the Wapping Wharf cargo containers.

m-shed.name: M Shed
m-shed.hours: Tue–Sun, roughly 10:00–17:00 · check on the day
m-shed.tip: Free museum of Bristol life on the docks; the cranes outside are a good photo stop.

clifton-village.name: Clifton Village walk
clifton-village.tip: Wander the Georgian streets and stop for coffee before or after the bridge.

bristol-cathedral.name: Bristol Cathedral
bristol-cathedral.hours: Daily daytime · check on the day for services
bristol-cathedral.tip: Look up at the unusual hall-church nave; quietest in the morning.

harbour-ferry.name: Harbour ferry ride
harbour-ferry.price_text: A few GBP per hop · check fares on board
harbour-ferry.hours: Daytime, roughly spring to autumn · check on the day
harbour-ferry.tip: A short boat hop between the harbour stops is a cheap way to see the docks from the water.

clifton-observatory.name: Clifton Observatory and Giant's Cave
clifton-observatory.price_text: Small entry fee · check on the day
clifton-observatory.hours: Daytime, weather dependent · check on the day
clifton-observatory.tip: The cave viewpoint over the gorge is the draw; paths can be slippery.

royal-crescent.name: Royal Crescent
royal-crescent.price_text: Not in Bristol · the Royal Crescent is in Bath — check before planning
royal-crescent.tip: This landmark is in Bath, about 20 minutes by train; plan it as a separate day trip.

severn-river.name: Severn River
severn-river.tip: The Severn meets the Avon near Bristol; the tidal bore is best seen from further downstream, check tide times.

roman-baths.name: The Roman Baths
roman-baths.price_text: Not in Bristol · the Roman Baths are in Bath — check prices online
roman-baths.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–18:00 · check on the day
roman-baths.tip: Book tickets online and go early; it is a day trip from Bristol by train.

university-of-bath.name: University of Bath
university-of-bath.price_text: Not in Bristol · campus is in Bath
university-of-bath.hours: Campus generally open daytime · check on the day
university-of-bath.tip: This is in Bath, not Bristol; only visit if you have a reason to be on campus.

university-of-bristol.name: University of Bristol
university-of-bristol.price_text: Free to walk the public areas
university-of-bristol.tip: The Wills Memorial Tower is the landmark; the area around it is a pleasant walk.

stays.why: Walk to the SS Great Britain, M Shed and the waterfront bars. Quiet at night but close to everything.
Central for St Nicholas Market, the harbour and Temple Meads. Best if you want to walk everywhere.
Leafy streets, the Suspension Bridge and the university. Village feel, 20–30 min walk or a short bus to the centre.
Cheapest and handiest for trains and coaches. 15 min walk to the centre; good for short stays.

food: Try a West Country pasty and a proper cider. Ask for dry or sweet; cider here is stronger than you expect.
St Nicholas Market in the Old City has cheap global street food at lunch, roughly £6–12 a portion.
Stokes Croft and Gloucester Road are the independent café and brunch strips. Expect queues at weekends.
Book ahead for dinner on Friday and Saturday. Popular Harbourside and Clifton places fill up.
Look for local produce: Somerset cheese, Severn salmon and Bristol-made beer. Check menus for what's in season.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for the Clifton Suspension Bridge and the Downs: walk or take a short bus, then tea in Clifton Village.
Take the train to Bath (about 15 min from Temple Meads) for Roman baths and Georgian streets. Check times on the day.
Head to the Severn Beach rail line for a half-day out to Avonmouth or the coast. Simple, cheap and car-free.
